questions.question: What is Enumerable and what are its common methods?
questions.title: Ruby Enumerable
questions.direct_answer: Enumerable is a module mixed into Array and Hash (and others) that gives you a large set of iteration methods: each (iterate), map (transform to a new array), select (keep matching), reject (drop matching), reduce (fold to one value), find (first match), sort, group_by, flat_map. You include Enumerable in your own class and define each, and you get all of them for free. They're the heart of Ruby's collection-processing style — short, expressive chains that replace most loops.

each/map/select/reduce and more — free once you define each.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
```

sections.title: Common Enumerable methods
sections.content:
```ruby
nums = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]

nums.each { |n| puts n }                 # iterate (no return value used)
nums.map { |n| n * 2 }                    # [2, 4, 6, 8, 10] (transform)
nums.select { |n| n.even? }               # [2, 4] (keep matching)
nums.reject { |n| n.even? }               # [1, 3, 5] (drop matching)
nums.reduce(0) { |sum, n| sum + n }       # 15 (fold to one value)
nums.find { |n| n > 3 }                   # 4 (first match)
nums.group_by { |n| n.even? }            # {true=>[2,4], false=>[1,3,5]}
nums.flat_map { |n| [n, n * 10] }         # [1,10,2,20,3,30,4,40,5,50]

# Include in your own class — define each, get the rest:
class Deck
  include Enumerable
  def initialize; @cards = (1..52).to_a; end
  def each(&b); @cards.each(&b); end   # now map/select/sort all work
end
```
